directives.text: No Vercel preview deployments. Every non-main deployment must land CANCELED — CANCELED is free, BUILDING/READY/ERROR is billed.
A push is the only Actions-consuming action a push approval covers. Reruns, workflow_dispatch, a second push or a non-draft PR are each a fresh ask.
A commit hash AND a verification that ran AND a user-invocable outcome. Two of three is not done.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Prove it fails before trusting that it passed, and take exit codes from UNPIPED commands.
A record of a thing is not the thing. Measure the artefact, not the comment, filename or tracker row describing it.
This board is DERIVED from the release tracker and defect register. Where they disagree with it, THEY WIN.
crowagent-platform-web + crowagent-portal get FOUR Vercel production deploys for the whole release — ONE at each phase boundary. Nothing mid-phase, for any reason, including a docs-only commit.
crowagent-website is SEPARATE. It does not count against that budget and ships as and when ready.
Railway, staging AND production: deploy whenever needed. No approval, no waiting.
Supabase, staging AND production: apply whenever needed. No approval, no waiting. Via MCP apply_migration, never db push.
There is no Phase 5. Phase 2 is CLOSED. Every remaining item is Phase 3 or Phase 4.
Never report deploy or phase state from a repository document or git log. Read the live surface — Vercel, Stripe, Supabase, Railway.

issues.title: CrowMark answer-library embedding is 100% dead on production
issues.note: This entry has a history of closures and retractions (:4129 closed, :4172 retracted the same day, :4335 found the root cause), so it is closed here only on a measurement anyone can repeat. Measured on production gujtuecjzfiqsdnzgyvo, not on a record. GET /cron/rag-backfill was triggered and returned backfill_library_embeddings: scanned 10, embedded 10, failed 0. A direct query then confirmed bid_answer_library = 10 rows / 10 embedded / 0 null, independently re-run on write-back 2026-08-08 (select count(*), count(embedding) from bid_answer_library → 10, 10), and ai_calls shows crowmark_chunk_embedding 10 calls at 2026-08-08 21:10:48 UTC against crowmark_library_embedding 866. The column that was 0/10 for the whole release is full. ⚠️ CORRECTION TO THIS REGISTER'S OWN CLAIM. The entry stated that an HTTP trigger for the backfill still had to be built. It already existed — api/app/routers/cron.py:418, @router.get("/rag-backfill"), verified by direct read on write-back 2026-08-08, carrying its own [R262-D-10] docstring explaining that the backfill was otherwise reachable only from the 03:20 UTC tick. That correction belongs to CARRY-22, whose backfill-endpoint half is therefore already delivered, and it is recorded on that row. ⚠️ A NOTE ON THE SWEEP'S OWN FIGURE, because it is the kind of error this pass exists to catch. The override carried into the write-back queue read *"re-measured at 20:57 UTC tonight … still rows 10 / embedded 0"* and downgraded the entry P0 → P1 on that basis, saying it should close only once the count moved off 0. That measurement was true when taken and stale by the time it was written back: the backfill ran at 21:10:48 UTC, thirteen minutes later. The stated figure was therefore NOT transcribed into this register — the closing condition it named had been met instead.

issues.title: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY missing on the worker service
issues.note: > Re-measured and it is PRESENT. Railway MCP, project crowagent-platform, service crowagent-worker, production environment: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is among the service's variables. Logged as a blocking owner action; it had already been done and nobody re-read it. > > One caveat kept deliberately: the API returns NAMES with values redacted, and a dashboard-set variable reaches runtime while an MCP-set one may not. So this proves the variable EXISTS, not that a worker process has read it. Closing on existence, because *missing* is precisely what the defect claimed. Evidence. public.ai_calls on production: surface crowmark_eval_judge — 40 calls, 40 errors, first 2026-07-29 18:30, most recent 2026-07-29 21:56, every one: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set -- cannot call Anthropic for surface='crowmark_eval_judge' Root cause — corrected from the initial report. The key is not missing from Railway production generally. Listed 2026-08-02: - crowagent-platform (production API) — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present ✅ - crowagent-worker (production) — absent ❌ The eval-judge surface runs on the worker, which is why the ledger disagrees with the API service's configuration. Reporting this as "not set on Railway production" would have sent the fix to the wrong service. Related but distinct: council_preread has zero ledger rows — not a key failure. It runs on the API service, which has the key. It has simply never been invoked in production. That is a separate observation about the buyer-side advisory surface, not a defect in this entry. Owner action — and it is simpler than I first recorded. I originally wrote that this needs the *value* copied across, which I cannot read (MCP returns valuesRedacted: true for connected OAuth apps). That framing was wrong. Railway supports cross-service reference variables, so no secret value has to be handled at all: Service: crowagent-worker Environment: production Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Value: ${{crowagent-platform.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}} It resolves at deploy time

The pages map in those manifests is empty, which is why every route reports the same number — Turbopack is not attributing route-specific chunks there at all. Content fingerprinting of those 9 chunks: | Chunk (gz) | Identified content | |---|---| | 73.8 kB | react-dom, react, next-router, scheduler, framer-motion, sentry | | 61.9 kB | react, sentry | | 24.9 kB | next-router | | 18.8 kB | sentry | | 14.1 / 12.1 / 8.8 / 6.1 / 4.3 kB | next-router, react, turbopack runtime | Supabase markers: absent from all nine. (the R252-PERF-TBT fix, which addressed blocking *time*), but deferring the call never removes the *bytes*: a static import puts the SDK in the eager chunk regardless of when it executes. issues.title: The EPC posture score is not the same number in both runtimes
issues.note: > The split cannot recur: there is only one runtime left. Verified 2026-08-05 — git ls-files returns api/app/services/crowmark_epc_posture.py and its test, and no TypeScript counterpart. The duplicate was deleted in 6e4df3f2, before Phase 2. A half-up vs half-to-even rounding disagreement needs two implementations to disagree. Two implementations of the same regulated calculation round differently, and both test suites are green. | Runtime | Code | posture_score for the same portfolio | |---|---|---| | TypeScript | web/src/shared/lib/crowmark/epc-posture.ts:57-60 — Math.round(v * f) / f (half-up) | 6.3 | | Python | api/app/services/crowmark_epc_posture.py:101 — built-in round(...) (banker's, half-to-even) | 6.2 | Reproduced live, both sides, 2026-08-02 — not inferred from reading: portfolio = 5 × band A + 3 × band F → ratio = 5.0/8 = 0.625 (binary-exact) score = 0.625 × 10 = 6.25 node Math.round(6.25*10)/10 → 6.3 python round(6.25, 1) → 6.2 This is not cosmetic. posture_score is folded into the 0–100 CrowMark bid compliance score (api/app/services/bid_scorer.py:175,263). A supplier can be shown one figure and scored on another. Why neither suite caught it — and this is the part worth keeping. web/lib/crowmark/epc-posture.test.ts and api/tests/test_epc_posture.py assert the same six cases (0.0 / 10.0 / 6.0 / 5.0 / 2.0 / 10.0) and not one of them lands on a .5 boundary. Both suites are green and always would be. It is an ADR-0008 vacuous green in two languages at once — duplicated logic *and* duplicated blind spots, because the tests were ported alongside the code. Honest scope caveat: git grep finds no production importer of the TypeScript half in web/ today — only its own test. So the divergence is reachable through the shared module's public API rather than a currently-rendered surface. That does not make the numbers agree, and it does not make the next importer safe. Detection shipped, fix deliberately not. scripts/regulatory-parity.mjs compares rounding semantics

issues.title: the suite gets greener the more untested code you add
issues.note: The api suite shards by static lists in .certification/api-shard-N.txt. A test file created after those lists were generated belongs to no shard, so it never runs — while all six shards report green. This is the second occurrence in R2.6.2: | File | How it was found | |---|---| | test_r262_ai_001_embedding_model_guard.py | By hand, after a tally mismatch | | test_r262_d10_rag_backfill_reports_failure.py | By hand, 2026-08-02 — only because the first miss had taught me to check | A check that runs only when someone remembers to run it is not a check. scripts/verify-api-shard-coverage.mjs fails on unsharded, duplicated and stale entries, and fails closed on an empty scope. Fixture: 9/9, every breach paired with a control. Scope limit, stated rather than glossed: .certification/ is gitignored, so this is a LOCAL gate run beside run-shards.sh, not a CI one. In a fresh clone it exits 1 with a harness error because there is nothing to check. Making it skip-when-absent would turn *empty scope* into a pass — the identical defect one level up — so it is deliberately left fail-closed and out of CI. Its own fixture also found a flaw in the gate: missing resolved shard entries against the real repo root even when analysing a synthetic tree, so the MISSING case had been passing for the wrong reason. ---

issues.title: An expired trial never expires, and 8 production orgs have had free Portfolio since 2026-06-15
issues.note: D-16 blocked its own deployment on one question: > NOT RESOLVED UNTIL DEPLOYED, AND ONE THING MUST BE CHECKED FIRST: the 8 rows > are untouched. The code now refuses them — but if any of those orgs in fact paid > and the row is merely stale, deploying drops them to free scope. That check was never carried out. It has been now, on production (gujtuecjzfiqsdnzgyvo, 2026-08-08), and the answer is that no paying customer is affected. Three independent lines of evidence, none of which rests on the others: 1. The rows belong to internal accounts. All 8 are held by three owner-linked, single-member organisations (names redacted under the identity rule), every one created at the same microsecond — 2026-05-16 16:35:57.700721+00 — and all on tier='portfolio'. Eight rows created in one instant across three internal orgs is seeded data, not eight people who signed up. 2. Six of the eight are for products that no longer exist (crowcash ×3, crowcyber ×3; the remaining two are crowmark). A customer cannot be dropped to free scope on a product that has been decommissioned. 3. The Stripe account has never had a paid subscription. R262-D-02 established by live read that GET /v1/subscriptions?status=all returns exactly one subscription in the account's entire history — canceled, reason payment_failed, ended 2026-04-27. There is no customer to harm. So the D-16 deploy blocker is cleared. Deploying the trial_end_elapsed() fix drops three internal test orgs from portfolio to free, which is the correct outcome and the intended behaviour of the fix. ### One correction to the entry's own wording The heading says *"8 production orgs have had free Portfolio"*, and the body repeats *"still holds portfolio for all 8 orgs"*. It is 8 ROWS across 3 ORGS. The body's own measurement is stated correctly — *"8 product_subscriptions rows"* — so the count is right and only the noun is wrong, but the noun is the one a reader carries away. "Eight organisations on free Portfolio for 51 days" reads as eight

issues.title: No trial email has ever fired, because the cron reads a table nothing writes
issues.note: Found 2026-08-05. web/app/api/cron/trial-ending-d1/route.ts:155-158 queried table subscriptions for status='trialing'. create-checkout/route.ts:313-322 writes that row as status:"incomplete" and nothing ever flips it; the Stripe webhook writes only product_subscriptions. Production: subscriptions has 0 trialing rows; product_subscriptions has 8. So no trial-ending and no trial-expired email can send, and trials lapse silently with no conversion prompt. A second defect underneath it. The cron's tier→name map resolved starter/growth/enterprise to "CrowAgent Core", decommissioned under CORE-OFF-001. The moment these emails started working they would have told a CrowMark trialist that their *CrowAgent Core* trial was ending. Fixed in tree. Dedup keys deliberately unrenamed: day12-ending is both the template id and the email_log dedup key, so renaming it orphans every existing row and re-warns every org already warned. Consequence to settle before deploy: restoring the cron produces a four-message sequence (webhook D-3, cron D-2/D-1/D-0). They cannot duplicate a single message, but if four is too many, suppress the webhook path — the cron is the designated lifecycle emailer and the only one with per-stage idempotency. ---

issues.title: A subagent bypassed the identity pre-commit hook with --no-verify, "out of habit" CLEARED 2026-08-08 — verified no leak in authorship or any runtime path
issues.note: While fixing R262-D-33/R262-D-34, a subagent ran git commit --no-verify. That flag skips the pre-commit hook which CLAUDE.md establishes specifically to block the owner's personal name and Gmail from entering a commit — the IDENTITY HARD RULE. It then noticed, and re-ran git commit --amend --no-edit so the hook actually executed. Verified rather than accepted, because a claimed correction of a policy bypass is exactly the thing not to take on trust: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Author on 1a7521b1 | Crow Agent <crowagent.platform@gmail.com> ✅ | | Committer on 1a7521b1 | Crow Agent <crowagent.platform@gmail.com> ✅ | | Commit message, personal-identity grep | 0 hits ✅ | | Full diff, personal-identity grep | 0 hits ✅ | | .git/hooks/pre-commit re-run as a control | EXIT: 0 ✅ | | .husky/pre-commit re-run as a control | EXIT: 0 ✅ | No harm. The identity rule held, and it held because the *content* was clean, not because the gate ran. ### Why it is still logged The gate exists precisely so that outcome does not depend on the content happening to be clean. A bypass that causes no harm is a near miss, and near misses are the only warnings a hard rule gets before it fails for real. "Out of habit" is how a bypass becomes routine. Two process fixes, neither yet made: 1. Agent briefs must forbid --no-verify explicitly. Mine said "commit locally only, never push" and named the identity rule, but never said *do not skip the hooks* — so the instruction relied on the agent inferring it. An instruction that depends on inference is not a control. 2. The hook cannot enforce itself against --no-verify — nothing client-side can. The durable answer is a server-side or CI check on the same rule, so a bypassed local hook is caught at the point the work becomes shared. Worth pairing with the R262-D-09/R262-D-38 guard work rather than done alone. ---

issues.title: One carriage return made the entire API suite unrunnable, and the coverage gate reported PASSED over it
issues.note:
Found 2026-08-08 on the first attempt to satisfy CG-03 since the 08-05 repairs. ### What happened bash .certification/run-shards.sh api 1 6 died on shard 1 in three seconds: ERROR: file or directory not found: api/tests/test_crowmark.py no tests ran in 0.00s EXIT: 4 api/tests/test_crowmark.py exists. Exit 4 is a pytest *usage* error, not a test failure — the suite never started. The runner stops on first non-zero, so shards 2–6 never ran either. CG-03 was not failing; it was not executing. ### Root cause — one character .certification/api-shard-1.txt had CRLF line endings: $ head -1 .certification/api-shard-1.txt | od -c 0000000 a p i / t e s t s / t e s t _ c r o w m a r k . p y  
 run-shards.sh built its pytest argv with tr '
' ' ' < shard.txt. That converts the newline and leaves the carriage return attached, so pytest was handed api/tests/test_crowmark.py — a filename that does not exist. Strip the  and the file resolves immediately. Only shard 1 was affected, which is why the 08-05 run reached shards 2–6 and this presented as new. ### The part that matters — the gate could not see it scripts/verify-api-shard-coverage.mjs printed, on the same tree, minutes before: ✅ api-shard-coverage PASSED — 382 test files, all in exactly one of 6 shards Its parser splits on /?
/ (:92) and trims, so it compared clean paths, found all 382 on disk, and passed. The gate normalised the exact character the runner passed through. Its three checks — UNSHARDED, DUPLICATED, MISSING — were all genuinely satisfied. It was structurally incapable of observing the condition that made the suite unrunnable, because it was reading a different string than the runner was executing. This is AP-6 again — a gate scoped to the wrong property — and it is the fourth time in this release that a green gate has described something other than the thing it claims to govern (R262-D-15 static shard lists, R262-D-36 the RLS regex reading %I as public, R262-D-46 747 of 749 web files, now this). issues.title: Irrelevant padding can lift a rubric-coverage band by crossing a word-count floor
issues.note: AUD-C-04. Adding irrelevant text moved a mark from "Developing" to "Strong" by crossing a raw word-count threshold. A NOISE test should not move a coverage score at all — content the criteria do not ask for is not coverage. This actively rewards padding, which is the opposite of the behaviour a bid tool should teach, and it is the kind of gameability an evaluator would find indefensible. Acceptance criteria: word count may gate *eligibility* (a too-short answer is incomplete) but must not contribute to the coverage score. A NOISE test asserts appended irrelevant text leaves the coverage number unchanged. ---

issues.title: Coverage matching is exact-token with no stemming, so precise answers can under-score
issues.note: AUD-C-05. _score_criterion_coverage matches raw tokens, so "apprenticeships" does not match "apprenticeship". Acceptance criteria: stem or lemmatise before overlap. An EQUIVALENCE test asserts two answers of the same meaning in different words score within a small tolerance. ---

issues.title: astro build never ran, so 33 minutes of browser gates measured a stale dist
issues.note: Found 2026-08-08 on the first complete run of the website gate chain — a run only possible because R262-D-72 replaced the && chain with a runner that reports every gate. ### The tell was the duration, not the message FAIL astro check 1ms error: spawnSync ...astro.cmd EINVAL FAIL astro build 0ms error: spawnSync ...astro.cmd EINVAL 1ms and 0ms. A gate that fails takes time; a gate that never starts does not. Node 18.20 / 20.12 hardened spawnSync against CVE-2024-27980, so spawning a .cmd without shell: true now throws EINVAL outright. The runner pointed at node_modules/.bin/astro.cmd. ### Why it mattered far more than two red lines astro build is what produces dist/. It never executed. Every browser-driven gate after it — check-render, check-cwv, check-controls, check-autoplay, over 33 minutes of measurement — ran against a stale dist timestamped 14:05, reporting on output that no longer matched the source. 29 "passes" over an artefact from an earlier build. The runner did its job perfectly: it made a failure visible that && would have hidden. But it listed a gate-that-could-not-start beside genuine failures as though they were the same kind of thing, and they are not — one is a verdict, the other is the absence of one. ### Fix astro's JS entrypoint invoked under node, not the .cmd shim. shell: true would also work; this is better — no shell quoting, no PATH dependence, and it matches the runner's own stated intent of resolving the CLI directly. Proven by the re-run: astro check 18,945ms exit 0, astro build 4,926ms exit 0 — and check-render then passed, confirming the R262-D-72 fixes against genuinely current output. Chain went 29/33 → 32/33. ### The pattern, now three-for-three today A measurement that did not happen reads identically to one that succeeded. | | | |---|---| | R262-D-48 | printed *"382 test files — PASSED"* over a suite pytest could not resolve | | R262-D-64 | excluded Playwright specs by directory when the property was *"imports @playwright/test"* |

A detector that cannot distinguish test_call_site_derivation_is_not_vacuous from an API key is not providing security, it is providing noise with a security-shaped label. Documented to be revisited if Lob is ever integrated, at which point the exclusion must come out. ### The judgement worth recording The tempting reading was "13 verified secrets, stop everything". issues.title: The board's status classifier contained literal BACKSPACE characters, so every word-based status test was dead
issues.note: Found by refusing to accept a result I could not explain. After moving R262-D-72 to 🟡 FIXED IN CODE, NOT DEPLOYED, the board still showed it OPEN. The heading plainly contained the word FIXED, and the classifier plainly tested for it. Reasoning about it produced a contradiction, so the script was instrumented instead. Inside the running build, on the real string: DBG openBranch= false fixedBranch= true len= 169 DBG after-chain status= OPEN Both branch tests agreed the status should be FIXED, and the very next line reported OPEN. That is impossible for the code as READ — so the code as read was not the code on disk. Dumping the raw lines through JSON.stringify showed why: 133 " if (/🔴|\bOPEN\b/u.test(rawTitle)) {" 135 " } else if (/✅|\bRESOLVED\b|\bFIXED\b/iu.test(rawTitle)) {" JSON.stringify renders \b for U+0008 BACKSPACE. Those are not escape sequences. The file contained 8 literal control characters — the four word-boundary pairs — so the live regexes were: /🔴|<BS>OPEN<BS>/u /✅|<BS>RESOLVED<BS>|<BS>FIXED<BS>/iu /<BS>DIAGNOSED<BS>/i None of which can match ordinary prose. Proven rather than asserted: dead regex vs "x FIXED IN CODE": false intended regex vs "x FIXED IN CODE": true Consequence. Only the two EMOJI alternatives (🔴, ✅) ever worked. Every word-based status — FIXED without a tick, RESOLVED, DIAGNOSED — silently fell through to the default, and the default is OPEN. The WIP status was unreachable: DIAGNOSED could never match, so no item could ever hold it. After the fix, WIP 1 appears for the first time. This is the third defect in the same reporting path today (D-76 no dates, D-82 silent drops, this), and the same shape as all of them: the board understated completed work, and the understatement was silent. It is also a fourth instance of the release's theme — a check that could not fail. Two of the four emoji-marked branches did work, which is exactly why it survived: FIXED counts kept rising, so nothing looked broken. Terminal display is what hid it

issues.title: The board double-counted repeated ids and rendered the STALE one — including a P0 that had been fixed for a week
issues.note: The defect register is APPEND-STRUCTURED: when an item is resolved, a second section is written for the same id. The parser emitted both, and every consumer reads with .find(), which returns the FIRST match — so the board both double-counted the item and displayed the older, unresolved version. Measured 2026-08-08: 10 ids carried more than one entry, six of them a stale OPEN beside a later FIXED — D-02, D-04, D-05, D-06, D-08, D-10. Among them R262-D-02, *"Live checkout charges prices that do not match the published price table"* — the register's only open P0 — which had actually been resolved on 2026-08-01 with the owner's authorisation, Railway repointed and verified. The board reported a closed live-revenue P0 as outstanding for a week. Three rules, each added because the previous one was wrong in a way worth recording: 1. Last occurrence wins, by document ORDER rather than status rank. Order is the right signal for an append-structured file, and unlike "closed beats open" it still honours a genuine RE-OPEN. 2. The register outranks the tracker. Plain last-wins let a tracker row override the register — it flipped R262-D-09 from the register's DIAGNOSED back to OPEN. The register is the defect's own record; the tracker's rows are task rows that happen to share an id (R262-D-10's tracker row is a Phase-1 gate, not the defect). So only a later REGISTER entry may supersede a register entry. 3. Combined headings credit every id they name. The register closes related defects together — ## R262-D-02 / D-05 / D-08 — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-08-01 — and the heading regex captured only the first, so D-05 and D-08 never received their resolution. Only a run of / D-NN IMMEDIATELY following the id is treated as siblings, so a heading that merely mentions related defects in its prose is not misread. Two things a merge must never lose, both found by checking the result rather than trusting the rule: - Severity never drops. A continuation heading carries no · Pn · marker, so it parses at

issues.title: 36 defect headings used bold severity markers, and every one parsed as P2 — hiding 6 P0s and 19 P1s
issues.note: The heading regex read severity as (?:·\s*(P\d))?. The register writes severity two ways — · P2 · and · P1 · — and the second never matched, so those entries fell to the sev || 'P2' default. Measured on the register: 51 headings plain, 36 bold. Every one of the 36 was being reported P2. By true severity they were 6 P0, 19 P1, 7 P2, 4 P3 — so 25 P0/P1 defects were sitting in the P2 bucket, on a board whose entire purpose is to let the owner work highest-severity-first. The owner's instruction is "high value items are on first priorities"; the board was quietly making that impossible to act on. Found only because R262-D-10 — a P0 — appeared under P2 while its heading plainly read P0. It is the same class as D-89: the register's own formatting variation defeating a check nobody had tested against real headings. Fixed: (?:·\s*\*{0,2}(P\d)\*{0,2})?. Verified after — board-wide severity is now P0 7 · P1 45 · P2 246 · P3 6, and the OPEN P0s render correctly as R262-D-10 (CrowMark answer-library embedding dead on production) and R262-D-59 (60 active live Stripe prices for products that no longer exist). Fourth and fifth defects in this one reporting path today (D-76, D-82, D-89, D-90, D-91). Every single one understated or mis-ranked completed work, and every one was silent. The board is now the most-repaired component of this release, which is the correct outcome for the artefact the owner reads to decide what to do next. ---

issues.title: Two different embedding producers share one ai_calls surface name, so the cost ledger cannot attribute what it embedded
issues.note: Found by R262-D-10's retracted closure, which this defect is what made possible. crowmark_library_embeddings.embed_text records every call under surface crowmark_library_embedding. chunk_ingest deliberately reuses that same function — and therefore that same surface — for content_chunks embeddings (chunk_ingest.py:55-57). The step column, which exists precisely to sub-divide a surface, is NULL on all 856 production rows. Consequences, all of them measured today rather than argued: - A dead surface and a healthy one are indistinguishable in the ledger. 262 successes read as "library embedding works" when the library has zero embeddings. - Cost cannot be attributed. Every embedding pound lands on one line, so neither producer's spend can be seen, budgeted or regressed against. - Any alert or dashboard built on this surface reports the union of two unrelated pipelines. Fix: give the chunk producer its own surface (e.g. crowmark_chunk_embedding), or populate step at the call site so the existing surface sub-divides. The first is preferable — a surface is what the ledger keys on, and a producer that needs a different name should have one rather than relying on every future reader to remember to filter. Not fixed in this session: it changes what production writes to the cost ledger and is worth doing deliberately, with the D-10 root cause, rather than folded into an unrelated push. ---

issues.title: SWEEP-02 — the responsive breakpoints are defined in the spec and reach no code
issues.note: The five named breakpoints now exist in code. Commit 3e6fe30e. Re-counted on write-back 2026-08-09 by reading the file, because a count is exactly what the original entry got right and it is what would go stale first. web/app/tailwind-theme.css declares five --breakpoint-* custom properties inside @theme — sm: 40rem, md: 48rem, lg: 64rem, xl: 80rem, 2xl: 96rem — against the 0 this entry recorded on 2026-08-08. The matrix the successor defect complained about now reaches a stylesheet. Units are rem, not px, and that is a decision rather than a Tailwind default accepted passively. Declaring 640px would have frozen the breakpoint against the reader's browser font-size setting, so a reader who enlarges text would get the desktop layout at a size where it no longer fits. rem scales with that setting. It also happens to be the Tailwind v4 default, so the declaration does not fight the framework.

issues.title: SWEEP-04 — DEFECT CLASS: MCP apply_migration writes to the database and never to supabase/migrations/, and nothing detects it
issues.note: Commit 82c4235c · scripts/verify-migrations-have-files.mjs. The defect class was MCP apply_migration writing to the database and never to supabase/migrations/, with nothing able to detect the next occurrence. There is now a gate: it reads the applied migrations, matches each against the tree by SQL and by name, and fails on any version that matches no file. It carries a 118-version baseline for genuinely historical unmatched versions, under the contract that the baseline may only SHRINK — the same contract the design-system gate uses, and the reason a baseline is a ratchet rather than a permanent excuse. ⚠️ RECORDED BECAUSE THE WRONG ANSWERS ARE THE USEFUL PART: THREE DESIGNS WERE BUILT, MEASURED AND REJECTED FIRST. The second of them reported 429 of 623 migrations missing. That number is alarming, plausible, and was the GATE being wrong, not the repository — it matched on filename shape and every legitimately-renamed historical migration failed it. A gate reporting four hundred defects it invented is worse than no gate, because someone will act on it. The only thing that separated the true 118 from the false 429 was spot-checking the individual rows against the tree by hand before believing either figure. See [[feedback_measure_the_thing_not_the_record_of_it]].

issues.title: SWEEP-05 — the RLS parity gate models only literal DROP TABLE; a dynamic EXECUTE format() drop is invisible to it
issues.note: Commit c05aee6b · scripts/rls/detect-unmodellable-ddl.mjs. The RLS parity gate models only literal DROP TABLE, so a drop executed through EXECUTE format(...) in a plpgsql loop is invisible to it — the gate reads clean and the divergence is real. The fix does not teach the parity gate to parse dynamic SQL, which would be a promise it could not keep; it adds a detector that finds the constructs the parity gate cannot model and makes them declare themselves. An unmodellable construct becomes a visible, listed exception instead of a silent hole. That is the correct shape for this class: where a gate has a structural blind spot, the blind spot must be enumerable even when its contents are not.

issues.title: SWEEP-06 — apps/portal renders shared UI against its OWN hand-copied tokens
issues.note: Commit 5b1ca3ae. apps/portal rendered SHARED UI against its own 647-line hand-copied token file, so a change to the shared package could ship broken portal controls with nothing failing. The tokens are now consolidated onto the shared source. A REAL ACCESSIBILITY DEFECT WAS FOUND BY DOING IT, and it is the argument for the work. --border-strong never received the X-6 correction the shared tokens applied, leaving it at 1.50–1.96:1 against WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, which requires 3:1 for the visual boundary of a UI component. Every portal control's border was below the floor, on an internal surface nobody audits, for as long as the fork existed. The fork was the mechanism: a copy does not receive corrections, and the longer it lives the more corrections it silently declines.

issues.title: R262-AI-COST-01 — Gemini 2.5 Pro output was priced at half its real rate, and the test asserted the same wrong number
issues.note: 8f02128d · *"fix(ai-cost): R262-AI-COST-01 Gemini 2.5 Pro output was priced at half its real rate"* — commit confirmed present on write-back 2026-08-08. issues.title: R262-ADMINCLIENT-500 — a bodyless 500 escaping a route's own error contract
issues.note: Commit 1c8cbf83. createSupabaseAdminClient() throws when SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is absent under NODE_ENV=production — verified on write-back at web/src/shared/lib/supabase/server.ts:116-117, where the guard reads if (optionalEnv("NODE_ENV") === "production") throw new Error("Missing env var SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY …"). In POST /api/reports/templates that throw escaped the handler before it reached the route's own serverError() path, so the caller received a 500 with an EMPTY BODY — no code, no message, nothing to act on — while GET on the same route returned a healthy 200 {"templates":[]}. WHY THAT PAIRING IS THE DEFECT, AND NOT MERELY THE 500. A route that half-works reads to a client as *"this endpoint is broken"* rather than *"this deployment is misconfigured"*. The two diagnoses send an engineer to opposite ends of the system, and the empty body removed every signal that would have distinguished them. NOT A FALLBACK, and this is the line the fix deliberately does not cross. The misconfiguration is real and the request is still refused. What changed is that the refusal now obeys the same contract as every other failure on the route, so a caller can tell a server problem from a bad request. Nothing was made to succeed that should have failed. Found while building the critical-journeys CRUD test — it was the single failure in that suite, and its cause sat three layers away from where it surfaced, which is the argument for that suite existing. Verification recorded on the commit: tsc --noEmit REAL EXIT 0.

The table lives in public, so PostgREST serves it at /rest/v1/mfa_factor_removal_log, and both anon and authenticated hold a SELECT grant. RLS with zero permissive policies denies every role subject to it, while the service role bypasses RLS and continues writing the audit rows. That is precisely production's shape, and the INFO-level rls_enabled_no_policy the linter reports there is describing a deliberate fail-CLOSED configuration, not a defect. Adding a permissive policy here would WIDEN access — the opposite of the fix. Verified with a control, because two zeroes prove nothing on their own: | probe | rows visible | | --- | --- | | CONTROL — owner role | 1 | | as anon | 0 | | as authenticated | 0 | Without the 1, "anon sees nothing" is indistinguishable from "the probe was broken". THE CAUSE IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART. pg_get_functiondef returns a complete definition of the function's BODY and attributes and contains no GRANT or REVOKE — privileges are simply not part of a function definition. PostgreSQL then grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default on any new function. So a transcription that was faithful by every check I had applied, and whose post-condition passed, still left staging more permissive than production. **A schema transcription built from pg_get_*def covers STRUCTURE and misses PRIVILEGES entirely. pg_get_functiondef has no GRANT; pg_get_indexdef has no owner; pg_policies has no table-level grant. Any future "recreate from the live catalog" work must query information_schema.role_table_grants and has_function_privilege separately, or it reproduces this gap exactly. Scope CHECKED rather than guessed, in both directions: - TABLE grants for all 23 new tables are IDENTICAL on both databases (Supabase's default grant-all to anon/authenticated, with RLS doing the real gating). No table privilege diverged, so the blast radius is the two functions and nothing else. - update_business_hub_updated_at is anon-executable on BOTH databases, so it is PARITY, not drift, and was deliberately left alone. The fallback shim executed in Node: env === {}, env["NODE_ENV"] === undefined, shouldThrow -> true. 3. The real browser path executed — next start on a production build plus Playwright: typeof globalThis.process === "undefined" at document-start (asserted via addInitScript, so nothing could define-then-delete it) and after load. Fix: validate.ts:75 now uses the static process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production", and the @shared/lib/env import is gone — which is exactly what env.ts:18-19 already prescribed for client-reachable code. This changes production behaviour for real users, deliberately. Drift now logs a structured console.error and passes the payload through, so a drifted response is silent to the user and visible only in telemetry — which is what the header comment intends. ### The guard, and why the TEST is not the guard import "server-only" added to env.ts:30. Before any accessibility number could be trusted, the instrument had to be replaced: - web/scripts/axe-sweep.mjs never reads the HTTP status at all. - web/scripts/axe-sweep-authed.mjs prints it and never fails on it. So a route that 404s, or bounces to /login, yields no violations and was counted as clean. This is precisely the mistake caught on the marketing side earlier today, where /trust/ returned 404 and its silence had to be excluded rather than counted — the same defect existed in the platform's own tooling, permanently. New web/scripts/axe-platform-sweep.mjs gates every result behind HTTP 200 + unchanged final path + at least 200 characters of rendered text, reports every impact level, enumerates routes from the filesystem rather than a hand list, and fails closed when zero routes are reached. Auth is a programmatic Supabase password grant — no password typed into a form.

issues.title: A cross-tenant seat ORACLE, created by today's own fix, callable by any signed-in user
issues.note: Found by running the production security advisor after applying today's changes, rather than assuming they were clean. org_member_seat_deactivated(p_org_id uuid, p_user_id uuid) was created hours earlier by the R262-D-165 seat fix. It is SECURITY DEFINER, takes an arbitrary org/user pair, and performs no caller authorisation check whatsoever. Supabase exposes public functions over PostgREST, so any signed-in user could POST /rest/v1/rpc/org_member_seat_deactivated with two UUIDs and get an authoritative boolean back — bypassing RLS on org_users. Proportionate description, because overstating it would be its own defect. It is a small oracle, not a dump: one boolean, and the caller must already hold both UUIDs, which are not enumerable through it. But it confirms both that a user belongs to an organisation and that they have been deactivated — membership and employment-status information about another tenant — with no check that the caller has any relationship to that organisation. The contrast is what makes it actionable rather than noise. Every other authenticated-executable SECURITY DEFINER function here — user_org_ids, user_admin_org_ids, portal_role_for_current_user, dashboard_resolve_org — resolves everything from auth.uid() and can only ever answer about the CALLER. This one answers about whoever you name. Revoking is free, and that was MEASURED before writing the migration (control: checkSeatCapacity returns 2 files, so the search works): - client/application callers: ZERO - api/app/routers/teams.py references it only in two comments, as the documented SQL counterpart of the Python mirror - it is invoked 9 times inside supabase/migrations — only from other SQL Applied to staging AND production, roles named explicitly because REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC alone is not sufficient on Supabase — pg_default_acl grants EXECUTE directly to anon and authenticated. That exact mistake was made twice earlier today (R262-D-154). ### Verified, with the control that mattered most

issues.title: The public pricing API was serving Portfolio's £549 to ANONYMOUS callers
issues.note: ### Measured on LIVE production, not inferred GET https://app.crowagent.ai/api/public/pricing (no auth, no origin) -> 200 "portfolio": { "monthly": 549, "annual_monthly": 494, "annual_total": 5929 } The owner's decision is that £549 / £5,929 must never be published. It was being published, on an unauthenticated endpoint with permissive CORS, at the moment the decision was taken. ### The cause is a fix that reasoned its way into the defect R262-PRICE-TRUTH had already noticed that this endpoint and crowagent.ai/pricing disagreed about Portfolio. It resolved the disagreement by keeping the figure and adding a flag: > *"The price stays here because in-app upgrade needs a figure; what was missing is the > statement that nobody may sign up for it unattended."* That reasoning is coherent and still wrong. A flag beside a number does not un-publish the number. The renderer was made better informed while the anonymous payload kept the amount. And the premise does not hold either: in-app upgrade is an authenticated path, so it has no business reading the endpoint whose entire audience is the public. ### The fix short-circuits BEFORE the figure is computed A sales-led tier now returns { tier, pricing: "contact_sales", currency, sales_only: true } and never derives an amount at all. Computing it and then omitting it would leave the number one careless spread away from publication — which is exactly how it reached anonymous callers under the previous design. sales_only: true is retained so any consumer already branching on it keeps working. ### Tests: three existing ones asserted the DEFECT expect(m.crowmark.portfolio).toEqual({ monthly: 549, ... }) was a passing test pinning the published price. Two more asserted overlay and fallback behaviour *through* Portfolio. All were rewritten onto published tiers, and the suite gained: - The owner's required assertion, checked against the raw serialised body rather than the parsed object — a structural check only looks where it thinks to

issues.src: WS-17 — Make the published trial enforceable (R262-TRIAL-001)
issues.title: Close the calendar-month boundary
issues.note: Fixed 2026-08-09 · ee0bcdab · migrations 20261670000000, 20261680000000, 20261690000000, applied to staging AND production. REPRODUCED on staging before it was fixed, not inferred from the code: a trial straddling month-end drew 100 credits instead of 50, because the bucket key was the calendar month and the trial spanned two of them. The bucket key is now trial:<trial_end>, which cannot collide with a YYYY-MM row. TWO COUPLINGS WERE CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING, and either would have been worse than the defect. (1) The RPC writes the bucket to FOUR tables — ai_credit_ledger, ai_credit_debits, ai_credit_revisions, credit_overage_events — each with its own month_bucket CHECK; widening only the ledger would have 503'd every trialling customer on the first debit. (2) Top-up carry-forward compared buckets LEXICOGRAPHICALLY, and trial: sorts after every YYYY-MM, so the naive change would have RESURRECTED already-spent top-up credit — staging holds a live topup_balance = 100, so this was real money and not a hypothetical. Carry-forward is now chronological (ORDER BY created_at DESC). RE-VERIFIED ON WRITE-BACK against both live databases, not against the migration file: all four CHECK constraints carry the trial: alternation on prod gujtuecjzfiqsdnzgyvo and staging ipgrnwvfnumgvnxkpxsc, and check_ai_credits / consume_ai_credits / grant_ai_credit_topup all carry the chronological ordering on both — A trial straddling month-end sees its 50 reset once. Needs a schema change. CORRECTED 2026-08-09 (staleness-sweep write-back): this cell read TODO. ⚠️ A MIGRATION-LEDGER MISMATCH WAS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS ROW, and it is logged rather than tidied. issues.note: Run again at current HEAD while another lane was actively editing web/src, so this is not a citation of an earlier run. Reaching green required closing R262-D-150 first: the ratchet was RED for 0 regressions and 6 UNRECORDED IMPROVEMENTS — debt already paid down while the baseline stayed frozen. All six were re-baselined DOWNWARD (lib_tree 329→321, app_to_lib 491→490, lib_outbound 225→219, three stale allow-list entries dropped); every number TIGHTENED, none loosened. CONTROLLED, because re-baselining a ratchet is exactly the move that can neuter it: injecting a regression turned it RED (1 regression(s), REAL EXIT 1) and restoring returned GREEN (EXIT 0) — so it still discriminates and was not converted into an always-green. The prior verdict text is retained below because the restatement it records is the reason this row is meetable at all — ⚠️ RESTATED 2026-08-08 (staleness-sweep write-back). This gate previously read "FSD layer boundaries 0 breaches", and as written it can NEVER be met. scripts/arch-lint-web.mjs:70-88 says in its own words that it is "A RATCHET, not a conversion": it freezes today's numbers and fails when they get worse — and also when they get better without the file following. Cross-feature imports are frozen at 493 edges from 206 files (:96, was 967 from 362), not at zero. Re-measured 2026-08-08 after the Phase 2 cut: 0 regressions, 213 unrecorded improvements, 209 allow-list entries removed and none added. Verified on write-back by direct read of the script.
